key_insight: Co-free Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn alloys retain roughly half as many cascade-induced Frenkel pairs as pure Ni and show less interstitial clustering than Mn-free comparison alloys.
engineering_relevance: These defect-production trends support evaluating Co-free alloys for nuclear structural applications, but do not establish long-term irradiation performance.
method: Molecular dynamics with a short-range-stiffened EAM-21 potential.
Compared five Co-free HEAs with Ni and three Mn-free alloys.
Calculated defect energetics and simulated 1,015 cascades at 5–40 keV and 300/823 K.
evidence_signal: At 40 keV, concentrated alloys retained 56–72 Frenkel pairs, about half the Ni count; interstitial clustering was 54–58% in HEAs versus 67–71% in Mn-free alloys and 82% in Ni.
watch_item: Results depend on the interatomic potential and describe primary cascade damage, not long-term defect evolution under sustained irradiation.
paper_title: Point defects and primary radiation damage in Co-free Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn high-entropy alloys from molecular dynamics
